extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners (Central Reexamination Unit), supervisory patent examiners, and patent practitioners preparing or responding to ex parte reexamination requests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining whether a request for ex parte reexamination raises a "substantial new question of patentability" (SNQ), and procedural requirements for issuing orders, denials, panel reviews, petitions, and processing of such reexamination matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check file history for previously cited/considered prior art ("old art")
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to grant a request for reexamination, the examiner should check the patent’s file history to ascertain whether any of the prior art now advanced by requester was previously cited/considered in an earlier Office examination of the patent (e.g., in the examination of the application for the patent, or in a concluded or pending reexamination proceeding). For the sake of expediency, such art is referred to as 'old art'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'old art' derives from In re Hiniker. Examiners must identify whether the art cited in the request was previously of record and where it was considered in prior proceedings; this informs but does not automatically preclude a finding of an SNQ (see subsequent entries on 'old art').

rubrics_metrics.name: Old art can be sole basis for SNQ after Nov 2, 2002
rubrics_metrics.description: For determinations on or after November 2, 2002, reliance on old art does not necessarily preclude the existence of a substantial new question of patentability that is based exclusively on that old art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the 2002 statutory revision (Public Law 107-273), whether old art supports an SNQ is a fact-specific, case-by-case inquiry. Old art may raise an SNQ where it is presented or viewed in a new light or in a different way, in view of material new argument or interpretation presented in the request. When an SNQ is found based solely on old art, include form paragraph 22.01.01 in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 22.01.01—criteria for using 'old art' as sole basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this form paragraph when the SNQ is based solely on patents and/or printed publications already cited/considered in an earlier concluded examination of the patent being reexamined. The statutory addition indicates 'The existence of a substantial new question of patentability is not precluded by the fact that a patent or printed publication was previously cited by or to the Office or considered by the Office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert correct bracketed language: bracket 1 may be 'substantial new question of patentability' or 'ground of rejection' depending on context; bracket 2 lists the old art basis; bracket 3 explains how/why the fact situation applies (e.g., old art viewed in a new light). This paragraph is used only the first time the already-cited art is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior adverse Office decision on same/substantially identical prior art generally indicates SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior decision adverse to the patentability of a claim of a patent by the Office based upon prior art patents or printed publications would usually mean that 'a substantially new question of patentability' is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a prior adverse decision could result, for example, from a reissue application abandoned after rejection without disclaimer. Examiners should consider prior adverse Office decisions as strong evidence bearing on SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior adverse final decision by Director/Board based on non-patent grounds not a basis for SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior adverse final decision by the Director of the USPTO or the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences on an application seeking to reissue the same patent will be considered by the examiner. However, to the extent that such prior adverse final decision was based upon grounds other than patents or printed publications, the prior adverse final decision will not be a basis for determining whether or not a 'substantial new question of patentability' is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish the grounds underlying prior decisions; only prior adverse decisions based on patents/printed publications weigh toward SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions in other cases involving same art—consider weight based on circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: While the Office would consider decisions involving substantially identical patents or printed publications in determining whether an SNQ is raised, the weight to be given such decisions will depend upon the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should analyze factual similarity and context before relying on such external decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of federal court decisions affecting SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: A final court decision of claim validity in view of the same or different prior art does not necessarily mean no SNQ is present; the Office's determination is made independently. A nonfinal holding of invalidity or unenforceability will not be controlling. A final holding of invalidity or unenforceability after all appeals is controlling on the Office and an SNQ would not be present as to those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may accord deference to district court factual findings but is not bound by court rulings on validity for SNQ determinations; see Ethicon v. Quigg for authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims considered are those in effect at time of determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of the patent in effect at the time of the determination will be the basis for deciding whether an SNQ is present (37 CFR 1.515(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner’s determination generally limited to claims for which reexamination was requested. If requester fails to apply art to certain claims as required by 35 U.S.C. 302 and 37 CFR 1.510(b), those claims generally will not be reexamined. The Office may nevertheless reexamine other claims at its discretion and may initiate reexamination on its own initiative (35 U.S.C. 303(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester must set forth pertinency and manner of applying cited art to each claim
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 302 requires that the request must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, the requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of such claims; failure to meet 37 CFR 1.510(b) generally results in those claims not being reexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not consider amendments/new claims in copending reexamination/reissue when deciding request
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and/or new claims presented in any copending reexamination or reissue proceeding for the patent to be reexamined will not be considered nor commented upon when deciding a request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where reexamination is ordered, the first Office action and subsequent prosecution should be based on the claims as amended by any copending reexamination or reissue proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary prior art sources and limited supplementary searching
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary source of patents and printed publications used in making the determination are those relied on in the request. The examiner can also consider any patents and printed publications of record in the patent file from submissions under 37 CFR 1.501 compliant with 37 CFR 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner believes additional prior art can be readily obtained to supply deficiencies in the prior art cited in the request, the examiner can perform an additional search limited to the area most likely to contain the deficiency and only where there's a reasonable likelihood such prior art can be found to supply the deficiency necessary to an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to order reexamination and SNQ purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO has the authority to order reexamination only in those cases which raise a substantial new question of patentability. The SNQ requirement protects patentees from having to respond to, or participate in, unjustified reexaminations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Patlex Corp. v. Mossinghoff for legal context; ensure SNQ determinations are well-founded to protect patentees' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision granting reexamination—required content
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for reexamination is granted, the examiner’s decision granting the request will conclude that an SNQ has been raised by (A) identifying all claims and issues, (B) identifying the patents and/or printed publications relied on, and (C) providing a brief statement of the rationale supporting each new question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must identify at least one SNQ and explain how the prior art raises it. Examiner should indicate initial positions on issues identified (without rejecting claims) so patent owner and requester can comment. Prior art relied on should be listed on proper PTO forms (PTO-892, PTO/SB/08A/08B, PTO/SB/42 or equivalent) and copies supplied only if not previously provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required particulars to show for each substantial new question (A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each SNQ identified, the decision should point out: (A) the prior art patents and printed publications which add some new teaching as to at least one claim; (B) what that new teaching is; (C) the claims that the new teaching is directed to; (D) that the new teaching was not previously considered nor addressed in the prior examination of the patent or a final holding of invalidity by the Federal Courts; (E) that the new teaching is such that a reasonable examiner would consider the new teaching to be important in deciding to allow the claim being considered; and (F) where the question is raised or where it is not clear that a reference pre-dates the patent claims, a discussion why the reference is deemed available against the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These six points must be explicitly addressed in the decision; see MPEP § 2247.01 for examples. Item (F) requires providing reasons for availability/antedating when dates are unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may adopt requester’s reasons in simple cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In a simple case, the examiner may adopt the reasons provided by the requester in the discussion of the substantial new question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if adopting requester reasons, the examiner must still identify at least one SNQ and include the required decision content and rationale; do not make statements deciding patentability at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not decide patentability in the decision on the request
rubrics_metrics.description: In the decision on the request, the examiner will not decide, and no statement should be made as to, whether the claims are rejected over the patents and printed publications. The examiner only decides whether there is an SNQ to grant the request to order reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid language that implies claims are rejected; limit the decision to whether an SNQ exists. Provide initial positions on issues only to solicit comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patent grounds (public use/sale/102(c)/abandonment) are improper for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If arguments are raised by a requester as to grounds not based on patents or printed publications, such as those based on public use or sale, or abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c), the examiner should note that such grounds are improper for reexamination and are not considered or commented upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite 37 CFR 1.552(c). These matters may be argued by the patent owner during the reexamination examination phase but are not grounds for ordering reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and statement/reply periods when reexamination ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: When reexamination is ordered, the patent owner will be given a reasonable period, not less than two months from the date a copy of the determination is mailed or given, within which to file a statement on the question, including any amendment and new claims. If the patent owner files a statement, the requester may file a reply within two months of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision must set forth the time periods for filing statements and replies. Note special dispatch rules and extension limitations (see separate entry on extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time and special dispatch rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted in reexamination proceedings because 1.136 applies only to 'an applicant'. 35 U.S.C. 305 requires ex parte reexamination proceedings "will be conducted with special dispatch" (37 CFR 1.550(a)). Extensions in reexamination are provided for under 37 CFR 1.550(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not grant 1.136 extensions; use 1.550(c) when appropriate and ensure special dispatch obligations are observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for decisions and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.01 should be used at the beginning of each decision letter (grant). Form paragraph 22.73 should be used at the end of each decision letter to provide correspondence/inquiry routing information. Form paragraph 22.02 should be used as the introductory paragraph in a decision denying reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill bracketed fields appropriately (e.g., examiner name and telephone number in 22.73). Ensure correct use of form language depending on whether granting or denying reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference before issuing grant or denial
rubrics_metrics.description: After the examiner has formulated a draft preliminary order (granting or denying reexamination), the examiner must inform the CRU Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE), who will convene a panel review conference. If the conference confirms the preliminary decision, the proposed order shall be issued and signed by the examiner with two other conferees initialing. If not confirmed, the examiner reevaluates and issues an appropriate communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2271.01 for panel composition. The panel provides quality control and concurrence on the decision to grant or deny reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to vacate ultra vires reexamination orders—acceptable grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181 may be filed to vacate an ultra vires reexamination order, e.g., where the order is not based on prior art patents or printed publications; all claims were held invalid by final Federal Court decision; reexamination ordered for the wrong patent; reexamination ordered based on a duplicate copy of the request; or the order is based wholly on the same question of patentability raised by prior art previously considered in an earlier concluded Office examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive Director determinations to institute reexamination are not subject to review by courts until a final agency decision; 1.181 petitions are limited to ultra vires circumstances. See In re Recreative Technologies for relevant precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedures and timing for 1.181 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a 37 CFR 1.181 petition to vacate is filed, the third party requester may file a single submission in opposition. Because reexamination proceedings are conducted with special dispatch, any opposition must be filed within two weeks of service of the petition on the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend prompt notification to CRU support staff and the CRU SPE by telephone and filing opposition by facsimile when possible. Filing of opposition is limited to a single submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling prior art submitted after the order
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior art citations under 37 CFR 1.501 submitted after the date of the decision on the order should be retained in a separate file by the CRU or Technology Center and stored until the reexamination proceeding is concluded, at which time the prior art citation is entered of record on the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2206 for handling and eventual entry of such references into the patent record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision denying reexamination—required explanations per cited reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner concludes that no substantial new question of patentability has been raised, prepare a decision denying the reexamination request using form paragraph 22.02. For each patent and printed publication cited, indicate why the citation is: (A) cumulative to the earlier-concluded examination's teachings; (B) not available against the claims (e.g., due to date or because it is not a publication); (C) not important to a reasonable examiner in deciding claim patentability even if available and not cumulative; or (D) cited in the patent record and barred by the guidelines in MPEP § 2242 subsection II.A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also respond to the substance of each argument raised by the requester that is based on patents or printed publications. Note that improper grounds (public use/sale/102(c)/abandonment) are not considered for reexamination (37 CFR 1.552(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and distribution of decision documents and prior art copies
rubrics_metrics.description: After the examiner prepares, proofs, and signs the typed decision, the reexamination file and decision are given to the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Legal Instrument Examiner for coordinating clerical processing. Technical support prints headings and makes required copies for patent owner and requester of any prior art documents not already supplied. The original signed copy and a copy of enclosed prior art is made of record in the reexamination electronic file. A copy of the decision is mailed to the patent owner and any third party requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required copies are provided only as needed (e.g., if not previously supplied). Follow CRU clerical procedures to maintain accurate record and timely notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision denying reexamination—processing consequences and file closure
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision denying a request for reexamination is mailed and CRU retains jurisdiction to await any petition seeking review. If no petition under 37 CFR 1.181 is filed within one month, the CRU processes the reexamination file to provide the partial refund set forth in 37 CFR 1.26(c) and gives the proceeding a 420 status. The concluded reexamination file (electronic or paper) containing the request and the decision becomes part of the patent's record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print and annotate PALM screens as indicated ('PROCEEDING CONCLUDED'), scan into IFW using miscellaneous letter document code, and ensure the patent record is updated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples should reflect correct application of criteria (illustrative precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples (e.g., MPEP § 2247.01) show how to articulate an SNQ: identify claims, state which references raise or do not raise SNQ, explain why (e.g., a teaching not present in prosecution and likely important to a reasonable examiner), and state which claims will or will not be reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use example language and structure when drafting decisions (grant or denial) to ensure required elements (claim identification, reference identification, teaching explanation, availability issues, and practical effect on which claims are reexamined) are present and clear.
